title: Azure Machine Learning Studio
description: Understand Azure Machine Learning, automated ML, pipelines, and managed endpoints for training, deploying, and managing machine learning models.

data.text: Azure Machine Learning is a cloud platform for building, training, and deploying machine learning models. It provides workspaces that organize your data, compute, experiments, and models in one place. You can work in Azure Machine Learning Studio, a web-based visual interface, or use the Python SDK for code-first development. The platform supports frameworks like scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and Hugging Face.

data.title: Enterprise-Grade MLOps
data.text: Azure Machine Learning is not just for training models. It also handles model versioning, deployment tracking, and monitoring after the model goes live. This end-to-end support is what separates an ML platform from a simple notebook environment.

data.title: Key Components
items: Workspace: the top-level container that holds everything for your machine learning project.
Compute: cloud resources like CPU/GPU clusters and serverless Spark used to train models.
Datastore: a registered reference to your data in Azure Storage so you do not hardcode connection strings.
Experiment: a collection of trials that train models and log metrics.
Model: a packaged trained model ready for deployment.
Endpoint: a live, scalable HTTP endpoint that clients call to get predictions.

data.text: Automated ML, or AutoML, tries different algorithms, preprocessing steps, and hyperparameters automatically. You provide a dataset and a target column, and AutoML returns the best-performing model. This is useful when you are new to machine learning or when you need a strong baseline quickly.

data.text: Pipelines let you chain together steps like data preparation, training, and evaluation. Each step runs on its own compute target, and you can reuse steps across experiments. Pipelines make it easier to schedule retraining jobs, run batch scoring, and collaborate with team members who each own different stages of the workflow.

terms.definition: The central Azure Machine Learning resource that groups experiments, datasets, compute, and models.
A feature that automatically selects algorithms, tunes hyperparameters, and returns the best model for a dataset.
A scalable HTTPS endpoint that exposes a deployed model for real-time or batch inference.
A reusable, orchestrated workflow that chains together data, training, and deployment steps.

data.title: Train a Model with Automated ML
data.description: Use the Azure Machine Learning Python SDK to run an AutoML classification job on a sample dataset.
steps: Create an Azure Machine Learning workspace in the Azure portal.
Connect to your workspace using Azure DefaultAzureCredential.
Load a CSV dataset and register it as a tabular dataset.
Configure an AutoML classification job with a target column.
Submit the job and retrieve the best model once it completes.
data.expectedOutcome: You can submit an AutoML job in Python, monitor its progress, and download the best-performing model artifact.

data.title: Azure Machine Learning at a Glance
points: Azure Machine Learning is a managed platform for building and deploying ML models.
Automated ML helps you find the best algorithm and hyperparameters without deep tuning.
Pipelines chain together reusable steps for data prep, training, and deployment.
Managed endpoints expose trained models through scalable HTTPS APIs.
data.takeaway: Azure Machine Learning removes infrastructure work so you can focus on data and model quality while the platform handles deployment, scaling, and monitoring.
